proposals.claim:
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $\xi\in k^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order, and fix a finite integral multicharge
$m_1,\ldots,m_\ell$. Write $S=\{m_j:1\le j\le\ell\}$.
Use the arbitrary-base presentations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] to define
$H_d^{\deg}$ by $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^{\xi}$ by
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$.
For $d>0$, every nonzero joint generalized weight in the regular module has
labels $\nu\in\mathbb Z^d$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ respectively
$\xi^{\nu_r}$, and
$$\min_{s\in S}|\nu_r-s|\le d-1.$$
Thus both algebras have finite joint spectral decompositions defined over $k$.

Use the directed line $i\to i+1$ on $\mathbb Z$, with $d_i=1$,
$Q_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $Q_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ and $Q_{ij}=1$ for
$|i-j|>1$. Define the rank-$d$ cyclotomic KLR algebra as the direct sum of its
finite-content presentations, with first-strand exponents
$\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. Every nonzero word idempotent satisfies the same
bound, so this rank algebra is a finite sum of finite-dimensional graded
content algebras. Any interval containing
$[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]$ gives exactly the same rank-$d$ algebra;
enlarging it introduces only zero word idempotents. Rank zero is $k$.
At level zero every positive rank is zero. This lemma supplies support and
finite windows; it asserts no Hecke--KLR isomorphism or basis correspondence.

proposals.claim:
Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. Equal-color dot-sliding constants for $\psi$ are $+1$. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.

proposals.claim:
Work over $\mathbb C$, assume AC as in the degenerate categorification
suppliers, fix any finite ordered integral multicharge
$\mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_l)$, and let
$\xi\in\mathbb C^\times$ be not a root of unity. Write $H_d$ and $H_{\xi,d}$
for the degenerate and nondegenerate cyclotomic algebras with roots $m_a$ and
$\xi^{m_a}$ respectively. Suppose isomorphisms
$\theta_d:H_d\longrightarrow H_{\xi,d}$ have actually been proved and preserve
all generalized residue-word projectors:
$\theta_d(e(\mathbf i))=e_\xi(\mathbf i)$ for every $\mathbf i\in\mathbb Z^d$.
This is an explicit hypothesis, not a claim that such isomorphisms have been
constructed here.

Let $\lambda$ be any $l$-multipartition of $d$. Let $S_m(\lambda)$ be the
intrinsic degenerate Specht obtained by ordered affine induction of the
ordinary complex Spechts evaluated at $m_a$. Let $S_\xi(\lambda)$ be the ordinary
Murphy cell Specht for roots $\xi^{m_a}$, converted from a right module to a
left module using the generator-fixing presentation anti-involution. Then
$$[\theta_d^*S_\xi(\lambda)]=[S_m(\lambda)]\quad\text{in }G_0(H_d).$$
Thus the transported simple labels $D_\xi(A)$ characterized by
$\theta_d^*D_\xi(A)\cong D_m(A)$ have exactly the same decomposition
multiplicities in these ordinary Spechts for every charged multipartition
label $\lambda=\lambda(B)$ of the source dictionary in its sorted-charge
convention. For an arbitrary charge order the class equality holds as written;
to use the source labels, sort components and their partitions together. This identifies standard
CLASSES, not necessarily modules or cellular-head labels. If the comparison
also intertwines the residue functors, its transported simple/projective
labels are the same ground-component crystal labels. All levels and ranks,
including level zero, and all supported consecutive residue cuts are included.
